papers.title: Glioma regulates GABAergic signaling to drive hyperactivity and tumor progression.
papers.title_zh: 胶质瘤调节GABA能信号传导以驱动多动症和肿瘤进展。
papers.abstract: Recent studies have identified bi-directional communication between neurons and glioma tumors as a key driver of hyperexcitability and malignant progression. Although much of this work has focused on the activity of excitatory neurons, the roles of inhibitory neurons remain poorly defined. Using in vivo screening approaches in autochthonous glioma models, we found that the loss of a γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporter (Slc6a1) enhanced glioma progression, promoted network hyperactivity, and influenced tonic GABA release by tumors. Mechanistically, we show that glioma tumors influence the activity of inhibitory neurons and that their subsequent stimulation suppresses tumor growth. Further screening of these phenomena identified diazepam binding inhibitor (DBI), a secreted negative allosteric modulator of GABA-A, as a link between glioma-related hyperexcitability and proliferation that functions through modulating inhibitory neuronal signaling. Collectively, our findings indicate that glioma tumors utilize multiple mechanisms to manipulate the activity of inhibitory neurons as a means to drive network hyperactivity, which ultimately facilitates malignant progression.
papers.abstract_zh:
最近的研究已经确定神经元和神经胶质瘤肿瘤之间的双向沟通是过度兴奋和恶性进展的关键驱动因素。尽管这项工作的大部分都集中在兴奋性神经元的活性上，但抑制性神经元的作用仍然不明确。使用本体胶质瘤模型中的体内筛选方法，我们发现γ-氨基丁酸（ GABA ）转运蛋白（ Slc6a1 ）的丢失增强了胶质瘤
进展，促进网络多动，并影响肿瘤的强直性GABA释放。机械地，我们表明神经胶质瘤肿瘤影响抑制性神经元的活性，并且它们随后的刺激抑制肿瘤生长。对这些现象的进一步筛选确定地西泮结合抑制剂（ DBI ）是GABA-A的分泌负变构调节剂，是胶质瘤相关的过度兴奋性和增殖之间的联系，
通过调节抑制性神经元信号传导发挥作用。总的来说，我们的研究结果表明，神经胶质瘤肿瘤利用多种机制来操纵抑制性神经元的活性，作为驱动网络多动症的手段，最终促进恶性进展。

papers.title: KCNH1 variants associated with neurodevelopmental disorders exhibit prominent gain of function.
papers.title_zh: 与神经发育障碍相关的KCNH1变异体表现出显著的功能增益。
papers.abstract: Pathogenic variants in KCNH1, encoding the human ether-á-go-go voltage-gated potassium channel (EAG1, KV10.1), are associated with the neurodevelopmental disorders Temple-Baraitser syndrome (TBS), Zimmermann-Laband syndrome (ZLS), epileptic encephalopathy, and other undefined neurodevelopmental disorders. Investigating the functional consequences of KCNH1 variants can provide information about molecular and cellular pathophysiological mechanisms and help guide therapeutic directions. In this study, we determined the functional properties of 26 disease-associated KCNH1 variants including three recurrent and six that were previously unpublished. Findings were compared to the wildtype (WT) channel along with six rare population variants. Our approach used automated patch clamp recording of heterologously expressed KCNH1 variants in both the homozygous state (variant alone) and the clinically-relevant heterozygous state (variant co-expressed with WT channels). We also examined the impact of alternative splice isoforms on functional consequences of specific variants. We demonstrated that the majority of disease-associated KCNH1 variants exhibit features consistent with gain-of-function including hyperpolarized voltage-dependence of activation, accelerated activation kinetics, or both that promote hyperpolarization of the resting membrane potential. By contrast, one unique variant discovered previously in an autism cohort had a depolarized voltage-dependence of activation and was associated with a depolarized resting potential in cells. Pharmacological testing of KCNH1 variants demonstrated differences in potency for channel block by imipramine and an investigational non-selective potassium channel blocker (LY97241) for specific variants. Collectively, our findings support gain-of-function as the most common, albeit not exclusive, molecular mechanism underlying KCNH1-related disorders and suggest opportunities for potential therapeutic drug repurposing strategies for these conditions.

papers.title: Groundbreaking Study Identifies Excess Epilepsy Burden and Inequity in Māori Children: Confirms WHO-IGAP Targets.
papers.title_zh: 开创性研究识别毛利儿童的过度癫痫负担和不平等：确认WHO-IGAP目标。

papers.title: Differences in Epilepsy Etiology, Type, Syndrome, and Severity Between Māori and Non-Māori-Non-Pasifika Children With Epilepsy in New Zealand.
papers.title_zh: 新西兰癫痫儿童中毛利人和非毛利人的癫痫病因、类型、综合征和严重程度的差异。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The World Health Organization's Intersectoral Global Action Plan on Epilepsy and other Neurologic Disorders 2022-2031 aims to minimize epilepsy burden, with an emphasis on Indigenous peoples. Māori, the Indigenous peoples of New Zealand, have a similar prevalence of treated epilepsy to non-Māori yet suffer an increased epilepsy burden. This study aims to describe epilepsy etiology, syndrome, and severity in Māori children compared with non-Māori-non-Pasifika children.
METHODS: Retrospective population-based study using the New Zealand Pharmaceutical Collection. Medical records were reviewed to compare epilepsy etiology, type, syndrome, and severity between Māori and age-matched and sex-matched non-Māori-non-Pasifika children (younger than 18 years) with treated epilepsy. Period prevalence of etiology was compared: logistic regression (odds ratio, OR) for comparisons of within-cohort proportions and Poisson regression (rate ratio, RR) for comparison of population prevalence.
RESULTS: Cohort of 337 Māori and 421 non-Māori-non-Pasifika children (female: 45.4% Māori and 46.6% non-Māori-non-Pasifika). The median age of first seizure was 3.0 years for Māori (interquartile range [IQR]: 0.9-8.0) and 4.0 years for non-Māori-non-Pasifika (IQR: 1.3-8.0). Māori children were more likely to live in high deprivation areas (quintile 5: 48.4% Māori vs 17.3% non-Māori-non-Pasifika). Māori children were more likely to have a preventable cause of their epilepsy than non-Māori-non-Pasifika children (RR: 2.32; 95% CI 1.41-3.80) and more likely to have a structural (RR: 1.43, 95% CI 1.04-1.97) or infectious (RR: 4.72, 95% CI 1.43-15.8) etiology. After adjustment for socioeconomic status and rurality, there was no longer evidence for a difference by ethnicity. Focal epilepsy was the most common epilepsy type (65.6% Māori and 59.4% non-Māori-non-Pasifika), followed by genetic epilepsies (20.2% Māori and 21.9% non-Māori-non-Pasifika). An epilepsy syndrome was identified in 26% of Māori and 36% of non-Māori-non-Pasifika children. Māori children were less likely to have a self-limited epilepsy syndrome (OR: 0.51, 95% CI 0.30-0.83) or developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (OR: 0.59, 95% CI 0.40-0.88) but more likely to have intellectual disability and epilepsy (OR: 1.65, 95% CI 1.18-2.32).
DISCUSSION: Health inequities exist for Māori children who are twice as likely to have preventable epilepsy than non-Māori-non-Pasifika children. This inequity is largely driven by socioeconomic status and rurality.
papers.abstract_zh:
背景和目标：世界卫生组织2022-2031年癫痫和其他神经系统疾病跨部门全球行动计划旨在最大限度地减少癫痫负担，重点是土著人民。毛利人是新西兰的土著民族，其治疗癫痫的患病率与非毛利人相似，但癫痫负担增加。本研究旨在描述毛利儿童癫痫的病因、综合征和严重程度。
与非毛利-非太平洋岛屿族裔儿童相比。
方法：使用New Zealand Pharmaceutical Collection的回顾性人群研究。 对医疗记录进行了审查，以比较毛利人与年龄匹配和性别匹配的非毛利-非疟原虫儿童（ 18岁以下）治疗癫痫的癫痫病因、类型、综合征和严重程度。 比较病因学的期间患病率： logistic回归（比值比， OR ）比较
队列内比例等式和泊松回归（速率比率， RR ） ，用于比较人群患病率。
结果： 337名毛利儿童和421名非毛利-非太平洋岛屿族裔儿童（女性： 45.4%毛利儿童和46.6%非毛利-非太平洋岛屿族裔儿童）的队列。 毛利人首次癫痫发作的中位年龄为3.0岁（四分位数间距[IQR] ： 0.9-8.0 ） ，非毛利人非太平洋岛屿人4.0岁（ IQR ： 1.3-8.0 ）。 毛利儿童更有可能生活在高度贫困中
地区（五分位数5 ：毛利人48.4%对非毛利人17.3% ）。毛利儿童比非毛利-非太平洋岛屿族裔儿童（ RR ： 2.32 ； 95 ％ CI 1.41-3.80 ）更有可能患有癫痫的可预防原因，并且更有可能患有结构性（ RR ： 1.43 ， 95 ％ CI 1.04-1.97 ）或传染性（ RR ： 4.72 ， 95 ％ CI 1.43-15.8 ）病因。调整社会经济地位和农村地区后，不再有证据表明存在种族差异。局灶性
癫痫是最常见的癫痫类型（毛利人65.6% ，非毛利人59.4% ） ，其次是遗传性癫痫（毛利人20.2% ，非毛利人21.9% ）。在26%的毛利人和36%的非毛利-非太平洋岛屿族裔儿童中发现了癫痫综合征。毛利儿童不太可能患有自限性癫痫综合征（ OR ： 0.51 ， 95 ％ CI 0.30-0.83 ）或发育性脑病和癫痫性脑病（ OR ： 0.59 ， 95 ％ CI 0.40-0.88 ） ，但
可能患有智力障碍和癫痫（ OR ： 1.65, 95% CI 1.18-2.32 ）。
讨论：毛利儿童存在健康不平等，他们患可预防癫痫的可能性是非毛利-非太平洋岛屿族裔儿童的两倍。 这种不平等在很大程度上是由社会经济地位和农村地区造成的。

papers.title: Internet Intervention for Functional Seizures: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.title_zh: 功能性癫痫发作的互联网干预：一项随机临床试验。
papers.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Functional seizures (FS) are a common and disabling presentation in neurology clinics, but evidence-based treatments are difficult to access in Australia and in many regions globally. A brief, scalable, internet-delivered intervention could narrow this treatment gap.
OBJECTIVE: To compare a self-guided and a therapist-guided internet-based intervention for FS, each delivered alongside standard care, with standard care alone.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a 3-arm, parallel, randomized clinical trial conducted between February 2022 and April 2024, with follow-up through to 12 months after randomization. The location was a specialist outpatient clinic in Melbourne, Australia. Included were adults (≥18 years) with a documented diagnosis of FS confirmed by video electroencephalogram monitoring and at least 4 seizures per month, excluding comorbid active epilepsy.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to a self-guided internet-based intervention plus standard care, therapist-guided internet-based intervention plus standard care, or standard care alone. Re-PROGRAM is an internet-based intervention developed for FS, comprising 5 structured sessions integrating lifestyle factors, seizure management techniques, and elements of cognitive behavioral, acceptance and commitment, and dialectical behavior therapy.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was monthly seizure frequency at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months after randomization, recorded by daily prospective seizure diary, with retrospective estimates used for incomplete records. Secondary outcomes included depression, anxiety, quality of life, psychosocial functioning, and somatic symptoms.
RESULTS: Of 220 individuals screened for eligibility, 107 (mean [SD] age 36.0 [12.4] years; 89 female [83%]) were randomized. Of these participants, 96 contributed to the full analysis set (29 self-guided, 34 therapist-guided, 33 standard care). The self-guided arm produced significantly greater overall reductions in monthly seizure frequency than standard care (rate ratio [RR], 0.35; 95% CI, 0.18-0.69; Holm-Bonferroni [HB] method P = .006), with sustained between-group effects at 6 weeks (RR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.76; HB P = .02), 6 months (RR, 0.31; 95% CI, 0.12-0.78; HB P = .04), and 12 months (RR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.16-0.78; HB P = .03). The self-guided arm also showed greater improvements in anxiety than standard care at all 3 time points and in depression and mental quality of life at 1 or more time points. The therapist-guided arm showed greater improvement in anxiety at 6 months, but reductions in seizure frequency did not reach statistical significance. Direct comparison between the 2 active arms showed no significant difference in seizure reduction (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.33-1.36). Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness of the primary findings. No adverse events occurred in any arm.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this randomized clinical trial show that in adults with FS, a self-guided internet-based intervention reduced seizure frequency and improved anxiety relative to standard care, offering a scalable option for patients unable to access specialist psychological care.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Identifier: ACTRN12622000262707.

1个月（ RR ， 0.31 ； 95% CI ， 0.12-0.78 ； HB P = 0.04 ）和12个月（ RR ， 0.35 ； 95% CI ， 0.16-0.78 ； HB P = 0.03 ）。自我引导组在所有3个时间点的焦虑改善也大于标准护理，在1个或更多个时间点的抑郁和生活质量改善也大于标准护理。治疗师指导的组在6个月时焦虑改善较大，但癫痫发作频率的降低没有达到统计学意义。

papers.title: Comparative efficacy of first-line antiseizure monotherapy in pediatric focal epilepsy: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
papers.title_zh: 一线抗癫痫单药治疗小儿局灶性癫痫的比较疗效：系统评价和荟萃分析的综述。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: First-line antiseizure medication (ASM) monotherapy remains the recommended initial treatment for pediatric focal epilepsy. Although several ASMs are available, uncertainty persists regarding their comparative efficacy, safety, and tolerability, particularly in children. This umbrella review aimed to synthesize and map the available evidence from systematic reviews and meta-analyses evaluating first-line ASM monotherapies for focal epilepsy, with a focus on informing pediatric treatment decisions.
METHODS: This umbrella review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidance. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses evaluating first-line ASM monotherapy for focal epilepsy were identified through comprehensive database searches. Data on study characteristics, patient populations, ASM comparisons, epilepsy subtypes, follow-up duration, efficacy, safety, and tolerability outcomes were extracted and synthesized descriptively. Evidence mapping was performed to summarize the findings, and potential overlap of primary studies across the included reviews was considered. Where available, outcome-specific certainty-of-evidence ratings reported by the source reviews using GRADE or CINeMA were also extracted and summarized.
RESULTS: Sixteen systematic reviews and meta-analyses were included, comprising randomized controlled trials and individual participant data analyses from pediatric and mixed-age populations. Frequently evaluated ASMs included carbamazepine, lamotrigine, levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine, valproate, phenytoin, and several newer-generation agents. Across the included reviews, no single first-line ASM showed consistent superiority for seizure control outcomes. Selected comparisons suggested tolerability advantages for lamotrigine, levetiracetam, and some newer-generation ASMs; however, these findings were not uniform across outcomes or reviews. Several comparative estimates were imprecise, with confidence intervals encompassing potentially clinically meaningful effects, and substantial heterogeneity was present across epilepsy subtype definitions, patient populations, follow-up durations, and outcome reporting. The frequent inclusion of mixed-age populations further limited the strength and direct applicability of pediatric-specific conclusions.
CONCLUSIONS: Current umbrella-level evidence does not establish clear superiority of one first-line ASM over another for seizure control in pediatric focal epilepsy. Importantly, the absence of statistically significant differences should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic equivalence, because several estimates remain imprecise and clinically meaningful differences cannot be excluded. Interpretation is further limited by the scarcity of pediatric-specific comparative data, the frequent inclusion of mixed-age populations, and methodological and outcome heterogeneity across reviews. Safety and tolerability should therefore be considered alongside efficacy when individualizing treatment selection. Well-designed pediatric-specific comparative studies using standardized outcome measures are needed to strengthen evidence-based treatment recommendations.
papers.abstract_zh:
简介：一线抗癫痫药物（ ASM ）单药治疗仍然是小儿局灶性癫痫的推荐初始治疗方法。虽然有几种ASM可用，但它们的比较疗效、安全性和耐受性仍然存在不确定性，特别是在儿童中。这项总括性综述旨在综合和绘制系统综述和荟萃分析中可用的证据，这些综述和荟萃分析评估一线ASM单一疗法的局灶性
癫痫，侧重于为儿科治疗决策提供信息。
方法：本综述是根据系统评价和荟萃分析首选报告项目（ PRISMA ）指南进行的。 通过全面的数据库搜索确定了评估一线ASM单药治疗局灶性癫痫的系统评价和荟萃分析。 研究特点、患者人群、ASM比较、癫痫
ub型、随访持续时间、有效性、安全性和耐受性结局被提取并描述性地合成。 进行了证据映射以总结研究结果，并考虑了纳入的综述中主要研究的潜在重叠。 在可能的情况下，还使用GRADE或CINeMA提取和总结了来源审查报告的结局特定的证据确定性评级。
结果： 16篇系统评价
纳入了荟萃分析，包括随机对照试验和来自儿科和混合年龄人群的个体参与者数据分析。经常评估的ASM包括卡马西平、拉莫三嗪、左乙拉西坦、奥卡西平、丙戊酸盐、苯妥英和几种新一代药物。在所纳入的评论中，没有单一的一线ASM显示出癫痫控制结果的一致优势。选定的比较建议
拉莫三嗪、左乙拉西坦和一些新一代ASM的耐受性优势；然而，这些发现在结果或综述中并不一致。一些比较估计是不精确的，置信区间包括潜在的临床意义的影响，并且在癫痫亚型定义、患者人群、随访持续时间和结局报告中存在显著的异质性。
混合年龄人群的使用进一步限制了儿科特定结论的强度和直接适用性。
结论：目前的保护伞水平证据并未证明一线ASM在儿童局灶性癫痫的癫痫发作控制方面明显优于另一线ASM。 重要的是，没有统计学显著性差异不应被解释为治疗等效的证据，因为仍有几个估计
不能排除不精确和具有临床意义的差异。解释进一步受到以下因素的限制：儿科特异性比较数据的稀缺性、混合年龄人群的频繁纳入，以及各综述的方法和结果的异质性。因此，在个体化治疗选择时，应考虑安全性和耐受性以及疗效。使用STANDA的精心设计的儿科特异性比较研究
需要采用rdized结果措施来加强基于证据的治疗建议。

papers.title: Clinical efficacy and cost-effectiveness of epilepsy surgery in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.title_zh: 低收入和中等收入国家癫痫手术的临床疗效和成本效益：系统评价和荟萃分析。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize evidence on clinical outcomes, direct surgical costs, and cost-effectiveness of resective epilepsy surgery for drug-resistant epilepsy in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).
METHODS: MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through May 17, 2026. Original studies from World Bank-classified LMICs reporting clinical outcomes and/or direct costs of resective surgery were included. Engel Class I favorable seizure outcomes at ≥ 12 months were pooled using a random-effects model with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman variance estimator, while cost data were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Ten studies involving 2587 patients from seven LMICs were included from 20 948 identified records. Direct surgical costs ranged from US$500 in Iran to US$14894 in Colombia in 2025-adjusted dollars, equivalent to 9.4%-271% of national GDP per capita. Across four comparative observational studies, surgery was associated with higher odds of achieving Engel Class I favorable seizure outcomes than continued medical management (pooled OR 22.51; 95% CI 11.17-45.38; p < 0.00001; I 2  = 9%). Favorable outcomes occurred in 52%-79.4% of surgical patients versus 7.7%-16% of medically managed patients. Two Thai studies reported conflicting cost-effectiveness results relative to the national willingness-to-pay threshold.
SIGNIFICANCE: Resective epilepsy surgery was associated with substantially better seizure outcomes in appropriately selected patients in LMICs. However, the observational clinical evidence and heterogeneous, limited economic data preclude causal interpretation and broad conclusions on cost-effectiveness across settings.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Epilepsy surgery can help people whose seizures remain uncontrolled despite medication, but access to surgery is limited in low- and middle-income countries. This review examined 10 studies involving 2587 patients from seven countries. Patients who underwent surgery were more likely to experience favorable seizure outcomes than those receiving medication alone. Surgical costs varied widely between countries, and evidence about whether surgery provides good value for money remains limited and inconsistent. These findings suggest that expanding access to epilepsy surgery may benefit appropriately selected patients, while further research is needed to understand its affordability and long-term economic value.

papers.title: Neonatal-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy: High genetic yield and long-term outcomes in a multicenter southern European cohort.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the genetic diagnostic yield, characterize the clinical and genetic landscape, and evaluate long-term epilepsy, neurodevelopmental, and survival outcomes in a strictly defined cohort of neonatal-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE).
METHODS: Retrospective multicenter observational study across tertiary epilepsy centers in Italy, Greece, and Spain. Sixty-two full-term neonates fulfilling ILAE 2022 criteria for DEE with seizure onset within the first 30 days of life and a minimum follow-up of 18 months were included. All patients underwent next-generation sequencing-based genetic testing. Genetic findings, clinical characteristics, and long-term outcomes were systematically analyzed.
RESULTS: A molecular diagnosis was established in 82.2% of patients (51/62), identifying variants across 29 genes grouped, for descriptive purposes, into four broad categories according to principal biological role. First-line whole-exome sequencing achieved higher diagnostic yield than targeted gene panels (88.9% vs. 41.2%), although this comparison was influenced by differences in testing era and strategy. KCNQ2 variants were the most frequent genetic cause (29.4%), and several treatable metabolic disorders were identified. After a mean follow-up of 11.9 years, 64.5% of patients had drug-resistant epilepsy and mortality reached 17.7%. Seizure freedom was achieved in a subset of patients, particularly those with KCNQ2-related DEE. Nevertheless, severe-to-profound intellectual disability affected 71.7% of evaluable patients and persisted even among those who became seizure-free, suggesting that neurodevelopmental outcomes are influenced by factors beyond seizure burden, including the underlying genetic disorder and other disease-related factors. However, the marked variability observed precludes any causal inference from these data.
SIGNIFICANCE: This large European cohort demonstrates a high genetic diagnostic yield in neonatal-onset DEE, supporting first-line whole-exome sequencing as the preferred first-tier genetic test. The persistence of severe neurodevelopmental impairment despite seizure control highlights the need for precision therapies targeting disease mechanisms in addition to seizure management.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: We studied 62 newborns who developed severe epilepsy caused by genetic changes, following them for up to 25 years. We found a genetic cause in over 80% of cases, and genetic testing that reads the entire genetic code was far more effective than tests that only look at specific genes. Although seizures improved in some children over time, nearly all had lasting intellectual disability regardless of seizure control. This suggests that the underlying genetic condition may contribute substantially to brain development in addition to the effects of seizures, although our study cannot determine the relative contribution of each factor.

papers.title: Caution with self-reported ADHD symptoms in adults with epilepsy: discrepancy between subjective perception and objective cognitive performance.
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: Beyond seizure control, additional health issues are increasingly recognized as important aspects in the care of people with epilepsy (PwE). Cognitive impairments and psychiatric comorbidities, including attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), are commonly reported in this population. However, the widespread use of self-report screening tools and readily accessible online questionnaires raises concerns about the validity of subjective ADHD symptom identification in PwE and the potential for overdiagnosis. Therefore, this study examined the relationship between self-reported ADHD symptoms and objectively assessed attention and executive functions in PwE.
METHODS: A total of 289 adult PwE were included. ADHD symptoms were assessed using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS v1.1) and ADHD self-report (ADHS-SB) based on DSM-IV (ADHS-SB/DSM-IV) and ICD-10 criteria (ADHS-SB/ICD 10). Cognitive performance was evaluated using the EpiTrack®, a neuropsychological screening tool assessing attention and executive functions (n = 129). Agreement was assessed using chi-square tests, McNemar tests, and Cohen's kappa.
RESULTS: ADHD screening positivity ranged from 14.9% to 21.8%, with 6.6% positive across all instruments, attention and executive functions were impaired in 41.9%. ASRS results showed weak agreement with ADHS-SB/DSM-IV results (κ = .248) and ADHS-SB/ICD 10 results (κ = .321). ADHS-SB/DSM-IV and ADHS-SB/ICD 10 results showed substantial agreement (κ = .702, p < .001). Positive ADHD screening was showed no meaningful association with attention and executive functions (κ = -.050 to .146). EpiTrack® performance correlated with higher seizure frequency and polytherapy (p < .05).
CONCLUSION: Subjective ADHD symptoms show limited overlap with objectively measured cognitive impairment in people with epilepsy. Attention and executive dysfunction appear to be driven primarily by epilepsy-related factors rather than reported ADHD symptoms, underscoring the need for comprehensive clinical assessment.

papers.title: The ongoing dilemma of immunotherapy in antibody-negative suspected autoimmune encephalitis-associated epilepsy: A retrospective cohort study.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluates immunotherapy in drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) patients with concern for autoimmune encephalitis-associated epilepsy (AEAE) but negative neural antibody testing (-Ab).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study, focusing on patients treated at our Epilepsy Monitoring Unit (EMU) from January 2018 to May 2022. Of 39 patients with DRE who received immunotherapy, 27 had clinical concern for AEAE. After excluding patients with absent or incomplete neural antibody testing (n = 7) or positive neural antibodies (n = 8), 12 antibody-negative patients constituted the final study cohort.
RESULTS: Among the final 12 patients, 41.7% were female (median age 43.5 years, IQR = 28.8-63.3). The median age of epilepsy onset was 39.5 years (IQR = 23.8-60.3), and patients began immunomodulatory treatment (IMT) at a median of 15.5 months after seizure onset (IQR = 12.8-21.8). Distribution of treatments was 41.6% both intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) and methylprednisolone (IVMP), 33.3% IVIG alone, 16.6% IVIG, IVMP, and plasma exchanges (PLEX), and 8.3% IVIG, IVMP, and rituximab. After a median follow-up of 25 months (IQR = 24-31.3), the majority (10/12) had non-sustained responses beyond 6 months, with only 2/12 showing sustained (>50% reduction in seizures) responses. Confounding factors (e.g., concomitant ASM addition/change, lack of temporal relationship to immunotherapy) were identified in both cases.
SIGNIFICANCE: The study reveals IMT has limited success in patients with DRE and concern for AEAE but Ab-. Critical evaluation of IMT is essential in suspected AEAE cases with Ab- to avoid unnecessary administration of potentially hazardous immunotherapy in patients who are unlikely to benefit.

papers.title: Pilot testing an epilepsy self-management and resilience smartphone application for adolescents and young adults in Uganda.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: People with epilepsy in Uganda face substantial barriers to accessing culturally relevant self-management support. We developed the Self-Management and Resilience Tracking Application (SMART App) to address this gap in existing epilepsy self-management tools by integrating routine epilepsy self-management support with resilience tracking and resilience promoting activities. The application was designed within Uganda's local cultural, social, and healthcare context. Pilot testing examined user engagement, usability, and participant feedback to inform refinement of the app in preparation for a future trial to demonstrate effectiveness.
METHODS: We conducted a 45-day mixed-methods pilot test of the SMART App among 60 adolescents and young adults with epilepsy in Uganda. The app is available in English, Luganda and Runyankore, two major local Ugandan languages. Engagement analyses were restricted to the first 30 days due to unreliable phone data availability for the final 15 days. Quantitative engagement measures were assessed using in-app usage logs. Usability was assessed using an adapted version of the Adapted Usability Scale. Pre- to post- changes in reported coping strategies, social support use, seizure-tracking habits, medication adherence, and stress-management were explored. Qualitative data were collected through individual interviews and focus group discussions (n = 56).
RESULTS: App uptake was 100 %, and no attrition due to non-use was observed. Over 30 days, the median number of unique login days was 20.5 (IQR, 8-25), and the median time from onboarding to last recorded use was 26 days (IQR, 22-28). Thirteen participants (21.7 %) had minimal use, 21 (35.0 %) moderate use, and 26 (43.3 %) high use. Feature uptake was highest for resilience tracking (91.7 %), followed by medication tracking (81.7 %) and seizure tracking (70.0 %). Usability responses were most favorable for ease of use, information retrieval, and user confidence, but were more mixed for learnability, organization, and intended frequency of use. Mean self-reported seizure-tracking scores were higher at follow-up than baseline (2.71 vs 3.32; mean difference 0.61, 95 % CI 0.15-1.07; P = 0.010), as were stress-management scores (2.98 vs 3.63; mean difference 0.65, 95 % CI 0.30-1.00; P= 0<.001). Participants shared how the app influenced their understanding of epilepsy, their evaluation of resilience features, and recommended additional tracking options, visual summaries, and expanded content. Participants illustrated the app's potential effects on epilepsy literacy and stress management, and to generate a more hopeful, contextualized understanding of epilepsy.
CONCLUSION: The SMART App demonstrated feasibility and high user acceptability with a particularly strong uptake of its resilience tracking feature. By integrating epilepsy self-management with resilience building support, the app offers a promising approach to addressing symptoms of distress, social isolation, and stigma among people with epilepsy. Findings support targeted refinement of app content and functionality, followed by prospective evaluation.

papers.title: Patient-reported adverse effects of selected newer-generation antiseizure medications: comparison of monotherapy and dual therapy in patients with epilepsy.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epilepsy is a common chronic neurological disorder primarily treated with antiseizure medications (ASMs), which may cause adverse effects that negatively affect quality of life. Using the validated Adverse Event Profile (AEP), a patient-reported measure of subjective treatment-associated side effects, this study aimed to compare the burden of subjective adverse effects in patients receiving monotherapy versus dual therapy.
METHODS: We analysed data from 259 patients treated at a German tertiary epilepsy center who completed the AEP questionnaire. Adverse effects under monotherapy were compared with those under dual therapy by evaluating individual AEP items, subscale scores, and total scores. Common monotherapies - levetiracetam (LEV), lamotrigine (LTG), brivaracetam (BRV), and lacosamide (LCM) - were compared with frequent dual therapy combinations (BRV + LCM, BRV + LTG, LCM + LEV, and LEV + LTG).
RESULTS: Overall, no significant differences in adverse effect burden were observed between monotherapy and dual therapy. Within the LEV subgroup, patients receiving LEV + LTG (n = 32) reported significantly higher scores for unsteadiness (p = 0.023), weight gain (p = 0.021), and memory problems (p = 0.009) compared with LEV monotherapy; no significant differences were observed for LTG monotherapy.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, dual therapy with newer-generation ASMs was not associated with a higher overall burden of adverse effects. Given the retrospective, cross-sectional design and small subgroup sizes, these findings should be considered exploratory and require confirmation in larger prospective studies. Unnecessary polytherapy should be avoided, and ASM treatment should remain individualised.

papers.title: Assessment of caregiver knowledge and attitudes toward pediatric epilepsy during an epilepsy monitoring unit admission.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caregiver knowledge and attitudes are critical to effective pediatric epilepsy management, yet misconceptions about seizure safety, treatment options, and long-term outcomes remain common. The Epilepsy Monitoring Unit (EMU) provides a unique opportunity for real-time education during diagnostic evaluation and clinical care.
OBJECTIVE: To assess changes in epilepsy-related knowledge and attitudes among caregivers of pediatric patients during a short-term EMU admission.
METHODS: This prospective pre-post observational study enrolled caregivers of children aged 2-18 years admitted to the EMU at Nemours Children's Hospital for epilepsy-related diagnostic evaluation or management. Caregivers completed the 16-item Epilepsy Knowledge Scale (EKS) and 14-item Epilepsy Attitude Scale (EAS) shortly after admission and again prior to discharge in English or professionally translated Spanish. Routine education occurred during bedside rounds without a structured study intervention. Paired analyses were used to compare pre- and post-stay scores, and item-level changes were assessed using exact McNemar tests, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Of 63 caregivers approached, 57 completed both pre- and post-surveys, yielding a response rate of 90.5 %. The mean EMU length of stay was 1.74 ± 1.29 days. Mean EKS scores increased from 7.33 ± 2.02 at baseline to 10.07 ± 1.83 at discharge, representing a mean increase of 2.74 points (95 % CI: 2.03-3.44p < 0.001) and an effect size of Cohen's d z  = 1.03. Median EAS scores increased from 39 (IQR: 35, 41) to 40 (IQR: 37, 42; p < 0.001; r = 0.48). Item-level results were mixed, and four of 16 EKS items remained significant after false discovery rate correction; no individual EAS item remained significant after correction.
CONCLUSIONS: Caregiver knowledge and overall attitude scores improved during a brief pediatric EMU admission. Because this was an uncontrolled observational study without a standardized educational intervention, the observed changes cannot be attributed specifically to routine education. Test-retest effects and language-related measurement differences are also possible. These findings support prospective evaluation of structured, standardized caregiver education integrated into EMU care.

papers.title: Cognitive effects of deep brain stimulation across targets in epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) affects one-third of individuals with epilepsy and increases cognitive decline. Resective surgery carries focal cognitive risks and contraindications. Deep-brain stimulation (DBS) represents a promising alternative, although its cognitive effects remain understudied.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane for pre- and post-DBS neuropsychological scores in DRE with ≥ 3 months follow-up. Fifteen studies (16 cohorts, n = 270) were reviewed; 12 (13 cohorts, n = 209) were meta-analyzed. Targets were the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT, k = 7), amygdalohippocampal region (AH, k = 6), centromedian nucleus of the thalamus (k = 2), and subthalamic nucleus of the thalamus (k = 1). Robust variance estimation computed Hedges' g by domain. Bias assessed with ROBINS-I and RoB 2; certainty with GRADE.
RESULTS: No cognitive domain declined significantly. Executive functioning was the only domain approaching improvement (g = 0.12, 95% CI -0.08 to 0.33), most apparent with ANT (g = 0.15, CI -0.16 to 0.46). Anxiety declined significantly (g = -0.36, 95% CI -0.68 to -0.04). Memory, language, processing speed, visuospatial functions, and global intellect remained stable. Cognitive adverse events occurred in 15.8% of patients, highest with ANT (20.1%) and lowest with AH (9.24%).
SIGNIFICANCE: Chronic DBS for DRE is cognitively well tolerated, with no decline across domains and emerging evidence of executive functioning and mood benefit, especially with ANT stimulation. Verbal memory and naming were preserved after AH stimulation, unlike dominant temporal resection. Plausible mechanisms exist for both cognitive improvement and decline, yet neither appears consistently on assessments. Whether this reflects true stability or insensitivity of current methods is unclear. A revised framework for assessment timing, domains, and metrics is recommended.

papers.title: Visuospatial attention modulates audiovisual temporal perception: Context-dependent associations between prestimulus alpha lateralization and perceptual reports.
papers.abstract: Audiovisual temporal perception depends on the timing of sensory events and on preparatory attention. We examined how visuospatial cueing affects explicit synchrony judgments and sound-induced flash illusions, and how prestimulus EEG relates to these perceptual reports. In Experiment 1 (N = 39), participants judged beep-flash synchrony across auditory- and visual-leading stimulus onset asynchronies (SOAs). In Experiment 2 (N = 36), they reported flashes in fusion and fission conditions across SOAs and corresponding references. Experiment 1 showed a Cue validity × SOA interaction, with more synchrony reports on valid trials at -100 and +50 ms. Cueing shifted the point of subjective simultaneity among 21 participants with reliable fits. Trial-level posterior alpha lateralization was associated with synchrony reports as a function of Cue validity. In Experiment 2, valid cues reduced raw fusion reports at -100, -50, and +100 ms. A Cue validity × SOA interaction persisted for reference-adjusted fusion scores, whereas neither raw nor adjusted fission showed a corresponding interaction. The association between reference-adjusted alpha lateralization and fusion reports varied with Cue validity and SOA, although a direct comparison with the visual reference did not establish an illusion-specific association. These EEG-behavior associations were stable after accounting for temporal progression, preceding trials, cue side, and an ocular-sensitive EEG proxy. Together, the findings indicate timing- and context-dependent effects of visuospatial attention on audiovisual temporal perception and identify preparatory posterior alpha lateralization as a correlate of subsequent reports.

papers.title: REFS: Robust EEG feature selection with incomplete labels for multi-dimensional emotion recognition.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Compared to single-type features, multi-type electroencephalography (EEG) features provide a multi-level representation for analyzing multi-dimensional emotions. However, the high dimensionality of multi-type EEG features, combined with the relatively small number of high-quality EEG samples, poses challenges such as classifier overfitting and suboptimal real-time performance in the multi-dimensional emotion recognition task. As the number of EEG channels increases, the issue will become increasingly severe. Moreover, practical applications of affective brain-computer interface frequently encounters partial absence of multi-dimensional emotional label data due to diverse emotional self-assessment models, and ambiguity and variability in individual emotion perception.
APPROACH: To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel robust EEG feature selection method for incomplete multi-dimensional emotion recognition. The method leverages adaptive orthogonal latent semantic indexing to reconstruct the multi-dimensional emotional label space through second-order and higher-order relations, which could reduce the negative impact of missing values and outliers on label reconstruction. Simultaneously, it employs least squares regression with graph-based manifold learning regularization and global feature redundancy minimization regularization to enable EEG feature subset selection despite missing information, ultimately achieving robust and fast EEG-based multi-dimensional emotion recognition.
MAIN RESULTS: The proposed method was validated on three multi-dimensional emotional datasets with varying channel configurations, namely DREAMER, DEAP and HDED, under different label missing ratios. Experimental results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms thirteen state-of-the-art feature selection methods in terms of robustness for EEG emotional feature selection across various missing ratios.
SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed method provides a robust and efficient solution for feature selection in multi-dimensional emotion recognition under incomplete EEG label scenarios, delivering reliable performance for practical affective brain-computer interface applications.

papers.title: Accurate EEG-based linear state-space model of cortical dynamics during a passive motor task with exogenous input.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Revealing the dynamics of the brain in the presence of exogenous inputs iscrucial for mechanistic understanding, interventions and regulations. We study state-spacemathematical modeling of brain's cortical dynamics using electroencephalography (EEG)data in an experiment with continuous exogenous input.
APPROACH: We use subspaceidentification techniques to model the brain dynamics in a passive motor task experiment.The EEG data were recorded while participants were seated with their wrist strapped to ahaptic manipulator. The manipulator imposed a continuous multisine angularperturbation to the wrist as the exogenous input to the brain.
MAIN RESULT: Using twosubspace identification algorithms, we show that linear time-invariant state-space modelsaccurately represent the measurements, in a latent space, assuming that the EEG data arethe models' output. The model is verified and validated using data from sevenparticipants. Moreover, we construct linear maps to relate the latent space dynamics tothe neural source space. We verify that the findings of our model align with thoseidentified in previous studies.
SIGNIFICANCE: Accurate linear model in the presence ofexogenous input provides a pathway for designing parsimonious and simple controllers. Inaddition, it enables development of online monitoring, connectivity analysis and controlrelevant to neurorehabilitation, motor learning, and brain-computer interfacing.

papers.title: Applications of functional ultrasound brain-computer interfaces in neurological diseases: research progress based on neurovascular coupling.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) bypass peripheral nerves and muscles to establish direct information pathways between the brain and external devices, providing novel approaches for motor function reconstruction, communication assistance, and neurorehabilitation in patients with neurological disorders. However, conventional non-invasive BCIs relying on modalities such as electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), or functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) exhibit limitations in spatiotemporal resolution, portability, or real-time capability. Functional ultrasound (fUS), an emerging neuroimaging technology based on neurovascular coupling (NVC), detects cerebral blood volume changes at a spatial resolution of approximately 100 μm; its imaging frame interval is 200-500 ms, whereas its effective temporal resolution, limited by the hemodynamic response, is 1-2 s, offering a potential solution to overcome these constraints. This review comprehensively analyzed NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces from the dimensions of technical principles, clinical applications, future directions, and challenges. fUS has demonstrated significant clinical value in stroke assessment, epilepsy monitoring, and early identification of neurodegenerative diseases. Emerging technologies such as transcranial focused ultrasound neuromodulation, sonogenetics, and intravascular ultrasound are driving the evolution of fUS from single-signal "acquisition" toward bidirectional "acquisition-modulation" closed-loop systems, which remain at the proof-of-concept stage. However, the hemodynamic response latency relative to neural electrical activity (1-2 s), the yet-unclear biosafety of chronic ultrasound exposure, and insufficient decoding reliability under pathological conditions remain critical bottlenecks requiring urgent resolution. In conclusion, NVC-based fUS brain-computer interfaces provide a novel tool for precision diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases. Future efforts should focus on conducting multicenter clinical trials and enhancing the robustness of decoding algorithms.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Acoustic Stimulation of Slow Oscillations Using a Wireless EEG Headband: A Polysomnography-Validated Feasibility Study.
papers.abstract: Acoustic stimulation precisely timed during sleep can enhance slow oscillations (SOs), a hallmark of deep sleep that is critical for restorative sleep. To date, this approach has largely been restricted to laboratory settings using high-density electroencephalography (EEG). Wearable EEG systems featuring closed-loop acoustic stimulation could enable scalable, home-based approaches to modulating slow-wave sleep. Here, we tested whether a real-time modeling approach (M-CLNS) could be implemented using a wireless EEG headband with forehead electrodes in healthy participants. Acoustic stimulation was delivered during a single night of sleep in alternating stimulation and sham conditions. We evaluated the accuracy of SO phase targeting utilizing the EEG headband and assessed whether it could be used to detect stimulation-induced changes in oscillatory dynamics. The findings were validated against simultaneous polysomnographic (PSG) recordings as an independent reference. We found that SO phase was targeted consistently near the intended phase using the headband, despite reduced amplitude and signal quality compared with simultaneous PSG. Acoustic stimulation produced an immediate enhancement of SO dynamics, as well as sustained increases in SO density and power spectral density within the SO and delta frequency range (0.75-5 Hz) during deep sleep. These effects were apparent both in the EEG headband and PSG signals. These results demonstrate the feasibility of closed-loop acoustic stimulation using a wireless EEG headband, providing a foundation for future home-based and clinical applications.

papers.title: Locomotor-State Dependence of Neuromodulation During Avian Free Flight.
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.abstract: Complex avian locomotor behaviors depend on the coordinated operation of neural processes involved in sensory perception, decision-making, and motor execution. Exogenous neural stimulation can alter motor output by intervening in neural processes, but its effects may depend on the current locomotor state. Here, we investigated the locomotor-state dependence of formatio reticularis medialis mesencephali (FRM) microstimulation in freely flying pigeons. Individualized stimulation parameters were screened under stable laboratory conditions and kept constant during free-flight experiments. Flight-state features before and during stimulation were extracted, and state-response models were constructed to quantify their associations with stimulation-evoked turning responses. Results showed that flight state during stimulation was more closely associated with turning responses than pre-stimulation state, with acceleration during stimulation making the largest contribution. When acceleration during stimulation was above the individual mean, turning-response dispersion decreased by 32.92%. In addition, pre-stimulation angular velocity was positively associated with acceleration during stimulation, indicating that the pre-stimulation locomotor state contains information related to the consistency of subsequent stimulation-evoked responses. These findings demonstrate that the effects of FRM microstimulation are locomotor-state dependent and provide a basis for identifying appropriate neuromodulation timing and improving response stability under complex locomotor conditions.

papers.title: Beyond Local Gating: Toward Network-State-Dependent Neuromodulation.
papers.abstract: Brain stimulation is progressively evolving from anatomically targeted interventions toward individualized, adaptive, and network-oriented approaches. Recent developments in brain-state-dependent stimulation have demonstrated that neuromodulation can be optimized by synchronizing stimulation with ongoing neural activity, while adaptive cortico-cortical paired associative stimulation (ccPAS) has extended this principle to distributed cortical networks. However, current approaches continue to define brain state primarily through local electrophysiological features, such as oscillatory phase or power, even though ccPAS is specifically designed to modify communication between interconnected cortical regions. In this opinion paper, we argue that the endogenous variable guiding ccPAS should instead describe the instantaneous physiological state of the targeted cortico-cortical pathway. We propose that online source-space functional connectivity provides a biologically meaningful and technically feasible estimate of this pathway state, thereby enabling a new framework of network-state-dependent neuromodulation. As illustrative applications, we consider pathways spanning different levels of experimental characterization, from established sensorimotor interactions to the less-characterized ventral premotor cortex (PMv)-posterior superior temporal sulcus (pSTS) pathway within the action-observation network (AON). This distinction highlights that the proposed framework is pathway-general, while its experimental implementation requires pathway-specific characterization of stimulation parameters and appropriate physiological readouts. In this framework, resting-state EEG is rapidly reconstructed in source space to estimate pathway connectivity, which is subsequently used to personalize stimulation targets and guide state-dependent ccPAS of a functionally defined cortico-cortical circuit. Finally, we discuss the technological prerequisites, methodological challenges, biological rationale, and open scientific questions that must be addressed before pathway-state-guided neuromodulation can be experimentally validated. We argue that redefining brain state as the instantaneous physiological state of the communication pathway targeted by stimulation may represent the next conceptual step in brain stimulation.

papers.title: [Mechanisms and outcome evaluation of neurofeedback in post-traumatic stress disorder intervention].
papers.journal: Sheng wu yi xue gong cheng xue za zhi = Journal of biomedical engineering = Shengwu yixue gongchengxue zazhi
papers.iso_journal: Sheng Wu Yi Xue Gong Cheng Xue Za Zhi
papers.abstract:
Patients with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) still face challenges such as limited treatment response in some cases and substantial inter-individual variability when receiving existing interventions. Neurofeedback (NFB), as a closed-loop neuromodulation approach based on brain-computer interface (BCI), can guide patients to regulate abnormal neural activity patterns by providing real-time feedback on brain activity features, and therefore shows potential for PTSD rehabilitation. This paper reviews the regulatory mechanisms of NFB on the prefrontal-limbic emotion regulation circuit and the dysregulated states of the default mode network, salience network, and central executive network. It compares three major modalities, including electroencephalography, real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging, and functional near-infrared spectroscopy, in terms of feedback targets, spatiotemporal resolution, and clinical applicability. Based on a multidimensional evaluation framework composed of clinical scales, neurophysiological indicators, and functional recovery indicators, this paper further discusses the clinical positioning of NFB relative to first-line treatments and the potential synergistic mechanisms of its combined application with psychological interventions. Current studies still face limitations such as insufficient control design and a lack of standardized training parameters. Future research should integrate individualized target selection and machine learning-based modeling to promote the standardized application of NFB.
创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）患者在接受现有干预时仍存在部分患者疗效有限、个体反应差异较大等问题。神经反馈（NFB）作为一种基于脑机接口（BCI）的闭环神经调控方法，可通过实时反馈脑活动特征，引导患者调节异常神经活动模式，在PTSD康复中具有应用潜力。本文综述了NFB对前额叶—边缘系统情绪调节环路，以及默认模式网络、显著性网络和中央执行网络失衡状态的调控机制；比较了脑电、实时功能磁共振成像和功能近红外光谱三类模态在反馈靶标、时空分辨率和临床适配性方面的差异；并基于由临床量表、神经生理指标和功能恢复指标构成的多维评价框架，讨论了NFB相对于一线治疗的临床定位及其与心理干预联合应用的潜在协同机制。当前研究仍面临对照设计不足、训练参数缺乏统一标准等问题，未来需结合个体化靶点选择和机器学习建模推动其规范化应用。.

papers.title: [Parkinson's disease state recognition based on local field potentials: An ensemble model with feature division].
papers.journal: Sheng wu yi xue gong cheng xue za zhi = Journal of biomedical engineering = Shengwu yixue gongchengxue zazhi
papers.iso_journal: Sheng Wu Yi Xue Gong Cheng Xue Za Zhi
papers.abstract:
Patients with Parkinson's disease exhibit differential local field potential (LFP) activities under different deep brain stimulation (DBS) conditions. To achieve a balance between the discriminative performance and computational complexity for the identification of DBS stimulation-related neural states, this paper proposes a feature-division ensemble learning framework. First, multi-objective feature selection was conducted based on stability, discriminability and parsimony to derive a compact feature subset from time-domain, frequency-domain and nonlinear features. Then, the three categories of features were assigned to their respective advantageous base classifiers and fused via hard voting. Window-level 10-fold cross-validation results on the public STN-LFP dataset from the University of Oxford demonstrated that the proposed model reached an accuracy of 97.18%, outperforming the support vector machine (88.85%) and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (92.84%). SHAP analysis revealed that β-related frequency-domain features and partial nonlinear features had relatively high contribution. The feature division strategy reduced the cumulative input dimension of the three base classifiers from 96 to 32 and eliminated redundant feature processing. This method can provide a reference for analyzing DBS stimulation-related LFP patterns and further research on closed-loop feedback biomarkers.
帕金森病患者在不同深部脑刺激（DBS）条件下表现出差异性局部场电位（LFP）活动。为兼顾DBS刺激相关神经状态判别的判别性能与计算复杂度，本文提出特征分工集成学习框架。首先基于稳定性、判别力和简约性进行多目标特征筛选，从时域、频域和非线性特征中获得紧凑子集；随后将三类特征分别分配给优势基分类器，并通过硬投票融合。基于牛津大学公开STN-LFP数据集的窗口级10折交叉验证结果显示，所提模型准确率为97.18%，高于支持向量机（88.85%）和极端梯度提升（92.84%）。SHAP分析表明β相关频域特征及部分非线性特征具有较高贡献。特征分工使三个基分类器的累计输入维度由96降至32，减少重复特征处理。该方法可为DBS刺激相关LFP模式分析及后续闭环反馈标志物研究提供参考。.
